decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary care item tightly linked to the installed base of wood floors, it preserves upside with little downside and offers no clear signal yet for abandonment.
A maintenance oil line fits the firm's core flooring system offer and aftercare logic, so keeping it open is attractive while market acceptance continues to be learned at relatively low cost.
This care line serves a specific oiled-floor segment and is still worth keeping as an option, though its narrower niche and some overlap with other care products raise the chance of later pruning.
An underlay with moisture protection extends the firm's flooring system proposition and likely has modest continuation costs, so management would keep it while demand information accumulates.
The high-density underlay foam is still worth keeping, but as a more commoditized accessory with potential overlap versus other underlays it faces a somewhat higher risk of rationalization.

An oak parquet line is close to the firm's core business and strategic capabilities, so despite higher carrying costs than accessories it is likely retained while the firm tests which variants gain traction.
